paragraphs.context: These characters are all descended from the ten
paragraphs.mainIdea: The children of the Red King.
paragraphs.simple: All the characters in the list come from the ten children of the Red King, a magician king who left Africa in the twelfth century (the 1100s) with three leopards.

background.note: A magician-king from long ago. His ten children each got a small part of his magic, and they passed it down to people in their families.

paragraphs.context: The Red King had already lived for several
paragraphs.simple: The Red King made a wonderful glass ball and put all the memories of his travels into it. He used it to travel through time, to the past and the future. In anyone else's hands it is dangerous.

background.note: This glass ball is the Time Twister. Whoever looks into it is carried through time.

paragraphs.context: Descended from a tribe who lived in the
paragraphs.simple: Asa's family came from a tribe in the northern forests who felt close to strange animals. Asa can turn into a beast when evening comes.

paragraphs.context: Descended from a man who conversed with ravens
paragraphs.simple: Billy's ancestor talked to ravens that sat on a gibbet. The people of his village sent him away for it. Billy can talk to animals and understand them.

paragraphs.context: Descended from a Scandinavian storm-bringer named after the
paragraphs.simple: Tancred comes from a storm-maker from Scandinavia (northern Europe). He can bring wind, rain, thunder and lightning.

background.note: The god of thunder in old Norse (Scandinavian) stories. Thursday is named after him.

paragraphs.context: It was January 1916 — the coldest winter
paragraphs.simple: The story begins in January 1916, in the coldest winter that anyone could remember.

background.note: In 1916 Britain was fighting in the First World War (1914-1918). Houses had no central heating, and many still used gas lamps.

paragraphs.context: At home, in a sunny house by the
paragraphs.simple: Henry's sister Daphne is very ill at home, so Henry and his brother James have been sent to stay with their uncle, Sir Gideon Bloor, so they will not catch the illness.

background.note: A dangerous throat illness that spreads from person to person. Before modern medicine, many children died of it.
Henry's uncle in 1916, the headmaster of Bloor's Academy. "Sir" is a title given by the king or queen.

paragraphs.context: Sir Gideon wasn't the sort of person you
paragraphs.simple: Sir Gideon is not a kind, warm man. He is the headmaster of an old school and he never lets anyone forget it.

background.note: The man in charge of a school (in America: the principal).

paragraphs.context: Bloor's Academy had been in Sir Gideon's family
paragraphs.simple: The school has belonged to the Bloor family for hundreds of years. It takes children who are good at music, drama or art, and also endowed children with strange powers.

paragraphs.context: He had reached his cousin Zeke's room. Zeke
paragraphs.simple: Zeke is Sir Gideon's only child, and Henry thinks he is the nastiest cousin anyone could have. Zeke is endowed, and Henry guesses his gift is a nasty one.

paragraphs.context: Henry opened the door and peeped inside. A
paragraphs.simple: In jars on the windowsill, pale things without a shape move slowly in a clear liquid. Henry is sure it is not water.

paragraphs.context: Aunt Gudrun came marching down the passage, her
paragraphs.simple: Zeke's mother is a very tall Norwegian woman with a lot of yellow hair and a big chest. Her long skirt hisses as she marches along.

background.note: The Vikings were sea-warriors from Norway, Denmark and Sweden over 1,000 years ago. Calling someone "a Viking of a person" means they are big and strong.

paragraphs.context: The Bloor family lived in the west wing
paragraphs.simple: The Bloors live upstairs in the west wing. The ground floor is a cold hall, a chapel, halls and classrooms full of old desks and dusty books.

background.note: The old part of Bloor's Academy where the Bloor family lives. A "wing" is one side part of a big building.

paragraphs.context: "Home is miles and miles away Jamie." Henry
paragraphs.simple: Henry tells James that home is very far away. He sits by the fire and seems to see their warm living room at home in the burning logs.

paragraphs.context: Henry hadn't noticed Zeke, but now he became
paragraphs.simple: Zeke sits silently at a table, thinking so hard about something in front of him that he does not move at all.

paragraphs.context: "Well, he was doing a puzzle. There were
paragraphs.simple: James says Zeke stared at the puzzle pieces and they moved together by themselves to make a picture of a ship. Some pieces would not fit.

paragraphs.context: without another word he picked up the single pieces, one by one,
paragraphs.simple: Without a word, Henry quickly puts the last twelve pieces in the right places.

paragraphs.context: James was too small to see the danger
paragraphs.simple: James is too young to see that Zeke is angry. He happily says magic doesn't always work and Henry is cleverer than Zeke.

paragraphs.context: With that remark poor James Yewbeam sealed his
paragraphs.simple: By saying this, James made sure that something bad would happen to Henry, and to himself too.

paragraphs.context: Henry descended into the hall. His collection of
paragraphs.simple: Henry's friends envy his marble collection. His father travels a lot and always brings home a new marble. They are made of different stones, glass and painted china.

background.note: Small balls of glass or stone. Children shoot one marble with the thumb to hit others. It was a very popular game in old Britain.

paragraphs.context: Henry decided to play Ring Taw his favorite
paragraphs.simple: Henry plays his favorite marble game alone. He draws two circles with chalk and puts thirteen marbles in a cross inside the small circle.

background.note: An old marble game. Players shoot their own marble (the "taw") at marbles inside a chalk circle to knock them out.

paragraphs.context: There was a light creak from behind him.
paragraphs.simple: Henry hears a creak. A tapestry seems to move. Behind it is a small door into the dark west wing.

paragraphs.context: In the passage behind the tapestry Ezekiel Bloor
paragraphs.simple: Hidden behind the tapestry, Zeke holds a lantern and a glowing glass ball full of swirling colors. He knows he must not look at it. It is one of the oldest marbles in the world.

paragraphs.context: On her deathbed, Zeke's Great-aunt Beatrice, a witch
paragraphs.simple: When his great-aunt Beatrice was dying, she gave Zeke the marble. She called it the Time Twister and warned him not to look at it unless he wanted to travel in time.

paragraphs.context: Ezekiel didn't want to travel. He thrived in
paragraphs.simple: Zeke loves his gloomy home and never wants to travel. But he wants to know what happens to someone who looks into the Time Twister, and he thinks Henry deserves it most.

paragraphs.context: Henry picked it up. He gazed into the
paragraphs.simple: Henry picks up the strange marble and looks inside. He sees gold domes, sunny cities and clear skies. Then he feels his body changing and knows he should not have looked.

paragraphs.context: Henry thought of his small brother. Would there
paragraphs.simple: Henry worries that James will be terrified if he sees his brother disappear. He decides to leave a message instead.

paragraphs.context: It was all Henry had time for. The
paragraphs.simple: Henry leaves 1916, the year he is eleven, and travels fast into a future time when most people he knows will be dead.

paragraphs.context: James sat rigid in his bed, too frightened
paragraphs.simple: James is too frightened to call out. Aunt Gudrun would be angry and Zeke would laugh at him. Only Henry would understand.

background.note: In British English "cross" often means "angry".

paragraphs.context: Before he had completely run out of tears
paragraphs.simple: The room gets warm and bright. James sees three glowing cats, orange, yellow and copper, walking around his bed.

background.note: These three glowing cats look like the Flame cats from book 1, which are linked to the Red King's three leopards.

paragraphs.context: Before the tears could fall again, the three
paragraphs.simple: The cats show James the words on the floor. But James cannot read yet, though Henry has been trying to teach him.

paragraphs.context: Obviously Henry wanted his brother to keep the
paragraphs.simple: James thinks Henry wants him to keep the marbles. The cats start to play with them.

paragraphs.context: Charlie Bone had been looking forward to an
paragraphs.simple: Charlie hoped school would not start in this weather, but Grandma Bone has destroyed that hope.

background.note: A British school year has three terms (parts). The new term starts in January after the Christmas holiday.

paragraphs.context: "No shirking for you," she said in her
paragraphs.simple: Grandma Bone says Bloor's opens whatever the weather. The bus will come at exactly eight o'clock on Monday.

paragraphs.context: Charlie was a weekly boarder at Bloor's Academy
paragraphs.simple: Charlie sleeps at Bloor's from Monday to Friday, so every Sunday night he packs a bag.

background.note: A pupil who sleeps at school during the week and goes home at the weekend.

paragraphs.context: "Pajamas, toothbrush, pants," Charlie muttered to himself I
paragraphs.simple: Charlie is not good at music, art or drama. He is at Bloor's because he is endowed: he can hear people in photographs. Grandma Bone and her sisters sent him there so his gift could be watched and trained.

paragraphs.context: Charlie held out the black-framed picture. It was
paragraphs.simple: It is an old brown photo with cracked glass: a family of five in a garden by a cottage, with a small sailing boat on the sea behind.

paragraphs.context: It was the mother who spoke first. Henry
paragraphs.simple: Charlie hears the mother telling Henry to stand still. She holds a small boy on her lap, and a girl leans on her knee.

paragraphs.context: A stiff white collar seemed to be giving
paragraphs.simple: Henry wears a stiff white collar, a tight buttoned jacket, short pants to the knee and shiny black boots.

background.note: Boys in 1916 wore short trousers that came to the knee, with long socks.

paragraphs.context: Uncle Paton was Grandma Bone's brother, but he
paragraphs.simple: Paton is Grandma Bone's brother, twenty years younger, and he has a good sense of humor. Lightbulbs explode when he is near, so he only goes out after dark.

paragraphs.context: Paton squinted at the family group. “Ah, that's
paragraphs.simple: Paton names them: the small boy is his father; the girl is Daphne, who died of diphtheria; the soldier is his grandfather, Colonel Manley Yewbeam; the woman is his grandmother Grace, an artist.

background.note: The First World War was going on (1914-1918). Soldiers sometimes came home for a short time "on leave".

paragraphs.context: "They were staying at Bloor's, Henry and James
paragraphs.simple: Henry and James stayed at Bloor's while Daphne was dying. In the middle of a game of marbles, Henry disappeared. Paton's father loved his brother very much.

paragraphs.simple: This is the same Ezekiel: Dr. Bloor's grandfather. He is still living somewhere in the academy with gas lamps and bad magic.

paragraphs.context: "He's a grand old fellow" said Paton. "He's
paragraphs.simple: Paton's father is in his nineties and still lives in the same cottage by the sea. Paton visits him every month, traveling at night.

paragraphs.context: Uncle Paton made one of his here-comes-a-bit-of-scandal expressions.
paragraphs.simple: Long ago there was a terrible quarrel. For Grandma Bone and her sisters, their father does not exist.

paragraphs.context: Charlie'd been put in the music department only
paragraphs.simple: Charlie is in the music department only because his father was. Fidelio is a brilliant musician, and seeing his friend's smiling face makes Charlie feel better.

background.note: One of the three parts of Bloor's Academy. Music students wear blue capes.

paragraphs.context: "I decided to change your name," said Olivia.
paragraphs.simple: Olivia has decided to call Fidelio "Fido" because Fidelio is too long to say. Fidelio points out that Fido is a dog's name.

background.note: A very common name for a pet dog in English-speaking countries.

paragraphs.context: Children in green capes had now joined the
paragraphs.simple: The art students are quieter than the drama students. But under their green capes you see sparkly scarves and gold thread, so you feel these quiet children break more serious rules.

paragraphs.context: The tall gray walls of Bloor's Academy now
paragraphs.simple: As Charlie walks up to the school, his eyes go to the window at the top of a tower. Like his mother, he feels someone is watching him from there.

paragraphs.context: As one of the smallest boys Charlie had
paragraphs.simple: Charlie stands next to Billy, a white-haired albino orphan. Billy ignores him. Charlie notices his new fur-lined boots, probably a Christmas present.

paragraphs.context: He was a big man with a lot of white, wiry hair.
paragraphs.simple: The head of music stops the hymn. He is a big man with wild white hair, and even the teachers are a little afraid of him.

paragraphs.context: Charlie realized that Mr. Pilgrim was not standing
paragraphs.simple: The piano teacher is sitting down. He never looks at anyone, never speaks and never shows any feeling.

paragraphs.context: The huge tree now lay halfway across the
paragraphs.simple: The huge old tree has fallen across the garden with its roots pulled out of the ground.

paragraphs.context: So many games had been played under its
paragraphs.simple: Everyone loved the tree. Now there is just snow, and a clear view of the red stone walls of the ruined castle, which look dark and threatening.

background.note: The old castle ruin in the grounds of Bloor's Academy. In book 1 Charlie got lost there and was chased by a beast.

paragraphs.context: As Charlie stared at the castle walls, something
paragraphs.simple: Charlie is sure he sees a small tree with red and gold leaves standing in the castle entrance, though other trees have no leaves now.

paragraphs.context: After assembly Charlie had his lesson with Mr.
paragraphs.simple: Mr. Paltry is an old, impatient flute player. Teaching Charlie the recorder is useless, he says, like filling a bucket with a hole in it. He even hits the recorder while Charlie is blowing.

paragraphs.context: Charlie didn't wait to hear the rest of
paragraphs.simple: Charlie runs away, remembering the night a yellow-eyed beast chased him through the ruin.

paragraphs.context: The sound of a hunting horn rang out
paragraphs.simple: A hunting horn tells the children that break is over.

background.note: In British schools, "break" is the short rest time between lessons when pupils go outside (in America: recess).

paragraphs.context: The temperature was still falling. After supper the
paragraphs.simple: After supper the twelve endowed children do their homework in the King's room. A nasty argument starts between Tancred and Lysander.

background.note: A round room at Bloor's with the Red King's portrait, where the endowed children do their homework.

paragraphs.context: Lysander silently shook his head, but unfortunately Zelda
paragraphs.simple: Zelda uses her power to move things: a big book flies off the shelf and hits Tancred in the back.

paragraphs.simple: In the cold hall, Charlie sees sparkling bits swirling in the air. Is it an ice storm?

paragraphs.simple: The marble that brought Henry is a Time Twister. Henry's mother told him about it. He knew Zeke would try to punish him.

paragraphs.context: Another two sets of stairs brought them to
paragraphs.simple: At the top of the tower, music lies all over the floor and the shelves are full of big books and old music.

paragraphs.context: In the King's room a boy with a
paragraphs.simple: Gabriel Silk worries about Charlie. Charlie is younger and the kind of boy that bad things happen to.

paragraphs.context: As he ran down the chilly stairwells and
paragraphs.simple: Billy is afraid of ghosts in the dark corridors. He has no home to go to, and only sometimes stays with an aunt.

paragraphs.context: Blessed considered this question. He seemed to be
paragraphs.simple: The dog says a boy came from nowhere with a small, shiny ball. Blessed doesn't like it: it is bad magic.

paragraphs.context: When homework was over, Charlie had half a
paragraphs.simple: Charlie doesn't like leaving Henry alone, nearly a hundred years from his own time. He badly needs to tell someone.

paragraphs.context: Mr. Boldova appeared. You could tell he was
paragraphs.simple: The art teacher's clothes are covered in paint. He looks as if he has just come back from a holiday: healthy skin, bright eyes and a long ponytail.

paragraphs.context: The three children slipped past him and ran
paragraphs.simple: It is nearly lights out. Matron will be angry and looking for trouble. Matron is Charlie's great-aunt, Lucretia Yewbeam.

background.note: The woman who looks after pupils' health and dormitories at a boarding school. At Bloor's, Matron is Aunt Lucretia.

paragraphs.context: The world had, indeed, changed. The sky above
paragraphs.simple: From the tower window Henry sees the sky glowing orange from streetlights, little lights in houses, and car lights moving like shooting stars.

paragraphs.context: In the distance a clock began to strike.
paragraphs.simple: The cathedral clock strikes twelve. Mr. Pilgrim turns to Henry with a strange shine in his eyes.

background.note: The big old church in the center of the city, with a clock and bells.

paragraphs.context: Mr. Pilgrim smiled. He stretched up to a
paragraphs.simple: Mr. Pilgrim offers Henry an oatcake from a tin. He almost lives in the tower and gets hungry.

background.note: Flat, dry biscuits made of oats, popular in Scotland and northern England.

paragraphs.context: All around the tower there was a steady
paragraphs.simple: The ice is melting. Henry works out that he arrived when the temperature was exactly the same as when he left in 1916. If the weather changes, he may not be able to go back.

paragraphs.context: Manfred Bloor had given Billy a present for
paragraphs.simple: Manfred gave Billy a powerful flashlight for Christmas, saying "We must keep our spies happy." Billy understood: he is a spy for the Bloors.

paragraphs.context: As Billy made his way closer to the
paragraphs.simple: Near the old man's room, nothing ever changes. Billy leaves no footprints in the dust, and cobwebs mend themselves after he passes. Ezekiel's magic, usually weak, works here.

paragraphs.context: Ezekiel Bloor sat in his wheelchair beside a
paragraphs.simple: The old man sits in his wheelchair by a big fire, wrapped in a sheepskin, with a skull-like face under a woolly hat. In spite of his fine clothes, Billy thinks he looks like a dead sheep.

paragraphs.context: "Charlie Bone," breathed Ezekiel. "Yes, yes, of course.
paragraphs.simple: Ezekiel understands that the boy is his cousin Henry, who looks like Charlie. That is why he can't stand Charlie. He orders Billy to find Henry.

paragraphs.context: "My cousin, yes. I sent him packing years
paragraphs.simple: Ezekiel sent Henry away into the future years ago. He mutters that the same cold temperature must have brought him back.

paragraphs.context: Ezekiel looked up. His small black eyes seemed
paragraphs.simple: Ezekiel tells Billy that the Time Twister is a crystal ball, not much bigger than a marble, that can twist you through the years.

paragraphs.context: Ezekiel grunted. He wasn't listening to the boy
paragraphs.simple: Alone, Ezekiel spits angry words into the fire. He throws in magic sticks to keep it burning, but they explode and fill the room with black smoke.

paragraphs.context: A bed creaked at the end of the
paragraphs.simple: Billy won the ruin game last term. His bronze medal gives him special rights and no detention for a whole year, so he won't be punished for being out at night.

paragraphs.context: Fidelio was also aware of Billy's intense stare.
paragraphs.simple: Fidelio's plan: Olivia will make a distraction to keep Manfred and Asa in the drama cafeteria, so Charlie can slip into the tower unseen.

background.note: At Bloor's each department has its own dining room, such as the drama cafeteria.

paragraphs.context: Each department had its own cafeteria, and the
paragraphs.simple: The drama cafeteria is the noisiest. The drama teachers allow strange hats, shoes and face paint. Manfred hates this, but he can't stop it, so he is hard on the music and art students instead.

paragraphs.context: Asa's yellow eyes took on a nasty gleam.
paragraphs.simple: They are not real friends; they stay together because everyone dislikes them. Manfred knows Asa can be dangerous: at night Asa can turn into a wild creature that Manfred can't control.

paragraphs.context: "Hold your horses, Manfred Bloor," said Cook sharply
paragraphs.simple: Cook tells Manfred to be patient. When he is rude to her, she makes him say sorry.
hardWords: Everything comes to those who wait

background.note: The cook at Bloor's Academy. Everyone calls her just "Cook". She is kind to the children.

paragraphs.context: At that very moment, Charlie and Fidelio were
paragraphs.simple: Charlie gets into the west wing. Fidelio guards the door: two taps mean Charlie is back; Fidelio will tap back if nobody is there.

paragraphs.context: Before he went into the dark passage that
paragraphs.simple: In the dark passage Charlie walks into a small thin figure behind a black veil. It whispers "Boy" and disappears.

paragraphs.context: Just before the horn went for the end
paragraphs.simple: Emma won't stay at school at weekends because she doesn't want to leave her aunt alone. Olivia is upset, because she helped rescue Emma from her horrible foster parents.

background.note: People who look after a child who is not their own. Emma lived with foster parents before she found her real aunt in book 1.

paragraphs.context: "Right, then left, then down the stairs," Charlie
paragraphs.simple: At midnight Charlie sets off for the kitchens, but his flashlight is weak and everything looks different in the dark. He gets lost.

paragraphs.context: Stumbling against chairs and tables, Charlie made his
paragraphs.simple: Charlie bumps through the cafeteria into the dark kitchen full of pans and machines. A pan crashes to the floor. Then he sees a light behind a door.

paragraphs.context: "I have come to the conclusion that I
paragraphs.simple: Henry thinks he came to this century because the weather was exactly as cold as when he left. Now it is warmer, so the Time Twister could send him anywhere.

paragraphs.context: "You could help me, Charlie. Just open the
paragraphs.simple: Henry wants to get into the freezer with the Time Twister, so that the temperature is right again. Charlie must check that he is still breathing.

paragraphs.context: The two boys swung themselves off the counter
paragraphs.simple: Charlie looks away from the marble, but the light on the ceiling shows golden domes, snowy mountains, forests, waves and a river of glass.

paragraphs.context: At the end of the corridor, several steps
paragraphs.simple: Cook's room is hidden behind closets. It is cozy: bright pictures, soft old chairs, a dresser full of gold cups and plates, and a warm black stove.

paragraphs.context: Charlie heard a faint meowing above his head.
paragraphs.simple: Three cats with glowing eyes look in through the glass in the roof. They are the Flames.

background.note: A window in a roof or ceiling.

paragraphs.context: The three cats leaped down from the chair
paragraphs.simple: The cats run around Henry's chair and rub against him. Charlie can hear tiny flames crackle as they warm him.

background.note: Here "the flames" are the three magic cats, Aries, Leo and Sagittarius. Their bodies give out heat and light.

paragraphs.context: Charlie looked up at Cook. For a moment
paragraphs.simple: For a moment Charlie sees a young, beautiful face behind Cook's old face. He has never felt as warm and safe as he does now.

paragraphs.context: "Me?" She smiled. "I'm the lodestone of the
paragraphs.simple: Cook says she is the "lodestone" (a natural magnet) of the house: she stops everyone flying off into the dark. She won't tell him her name yet.

paragraphs.context: "If you give the game away there'll be
paragraphs.simple: If Blessed tells anyone about Henry, he will get no more chops, no bed by the stove and no walks. He'll be thrown out.
hardWords: out of the goodness of my heart

paragraphs.context: For instance, there was a row of paintings
paragraphs.simple: With Cook's flashlight Charlie sees things he never saw before: paintings, boots and shoes outside doors, a plant in a china pot. Some of them were not there before.

paragraphs.context: Charlie wondered who had been giving Billy cocoa
paragraphs.simple: Charlie guesses that someone gives Billy cocoa as a reward for spying. Blessed saw Henry in Cook's room, and Billy understands the dog, so soon that person will know about Henry.

paragraphs.context: Breakfast was almost over when a violent gust
paragraphs.simple: A wild wind roars into the dining hall. Cups, plates, knives and spoons fly through the air, and children hide under the tables.

paragraphs.context: The race to reach Tancred was now even
paragraphs.simple: If Manfred reaches Tancred first, he may hypnotize him for a long time, as Emma was put to sleep for eight years.

paragraphs.context: Manfred had almost reached the stormy boy when
paragraphs.simple: Tancred sends a bolt of electricity at Manfred, which throws him across the floor. The great doors crack and fly open, and Tancred walks out.

paragraphs.context: "He won't be," said Fidelio confidently "The endowed
paragraphs.simple: Fidelio says endowed children are never expelled. Tancred will calm down and come back.

background.note: Sent away from a school forever as a punishment.

paragraphs.context: Gabriel nodded. "It's not far from where I
paragraphs.simple: Gabriel wants Charlie to come with him to Tancred's home, called Thunder House. It is a stormy place.

background.note: Tancred Torsson's family home. His father's moods make storms too.

paragraphs.context: "Too right." Lysander slumped in his chair. “And
paragraphs.simple: Lysander forgot that Tancred can't change the temperature, and Tancred hit the roof. Lysander thinks Manfred's stare made him forget.

paragraphs.context: "It's the glove. You know Gabriel's gift. He
paragraphs.simple: Gabriel can feel what happened to people who wore clothes before him. Now he has put on the glove.

paragraphs.context: Charlie tugged the fingers of the glove while
paragraphs.simple: Gabriel feels great pain. He says a woman put her fingers on a door and someone slammed it on them.

paragraphs.context: "A woman, I think. Yes, a woman. She
paragraphs.simple: Gabriel thinks the boy who crushed the woman's fingers was Manfred, but a smaller Manfred.

paragraphs.context: Behind Dr. Bloor a man with a deep
paragraphs.simple: Mr. Albert Tuccini, a sun-tanned man with a sad face, sits at the piano. He keeps looking at the curtains at the back of the stage.

paragraphs.context: The pianist's second piece seemed familiar to Charlie.
paragraphs.simple: The music seems familiar. Charlie falls asleep and dreams of a white room with his father at a piano, but he can't see his face. Grandma Bone hid or destroyed every photo of her son.
hardWords: at the back of his mind

paragraphs.context: "Is," said Gabriel. "She's still here. I've seen
paragraphs.simple: Gabriel says the glove belongs to the dark lady from the tower. She is not a ghost, just sad and alone.

paragraphs.context: I'll have you know that the dark lady is Mrs. Bloor.
paragraphs.simple: Cook tells them the glove belongs to Dorothy, the "dark lady": she is Mrs. Bloor, Manfred's mother.
